requirement_text: Before applying, applicants must have already taken a selection test (Bocconi online test/Bocconi online test - Law, SAT/LSAT or ACT) and obtained a score.
researcher_notes: Per the brief's instruction to record test name and administering body: Bocconi accepts either its own test (Bocconi online test, or the Law-specific variant) or external US-administered tests (SAT/College Board, LSAT, ACT) as alternatives -- test must be completed and scored BEFORE the application itself is submitted, not concurrently. Content extracted via a JS-triggered accordion expansion (the site's real content, not fabricated -- the plain HTML/text response does not include this section until the accordion control is activated, the same content a human visitor would see after clicking).

requirement_text: Even if they have taken a selection test, candidates are not automatically signed up for the upcoming selection session. This means that it's the candidate's responsibility to decide whether or not to apply in the upcoming selection session and with which test score. Test scores will not be automatically acquired from the webtesting platform.
researcher_notes: Procedural nuance: taking the test and applying are two separate, non-automatic steps.

requirement_text: Students already enrolled in a Bocconi undergraduate program may not submit a new application in a subsequent selection round unless they have previously withdrawn from their current enrollment. In the absence of such withdrawal, any application submitted in a subsequent round will be cancelled ex officio and will not be considered; the existing enrollment will remain valid.

International applicants who have graduated or transferred (as already enrolled) from Italian or foreign universities and wish to request recognition of credits already earned during other academic paths for a career abbreviation, will participate in a dedicated selection session. They can submit an admission application only from 25 November 2026 to 26 January 2027.
researcher_notes: A distinct, dedicated admission track for transfer/credit-recognition applicants, separate from standard first-time freshman applicants.
